title: NorthStar POC: Hosting options analysis and hybrid fallback plan (draft)
body:
Purpose
Quick analysis for the NorthStar retail POC: compare Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment paths and propose a hybrid fallback architecture that meets the customer’s low-latency checkout use case while keeping costs predictable during scale. This is a working draft intended for the upcoming design review (12/09).

Customer context and constraints (NorthStar)
- Industry: large omnichannel retail (customer-facing chat + fraud/risk scoring in checkout).
- Traffic: bursty peak during flash sales, baseline 80 RPS, peak up to 1400 RPS for short windows (5–20 min).
- Latency requirement: 95th p95 <= 120ms for token-limited assistant replies; critical checkout scoring p99 <= 200ms.
- Data residency: EU-only for customer data, PII must not leave customer VPC for private deployment mode.
- Compliance: requires SOC2 + contractual audit logs; optional HSM for keys.
- Budget target: <1.7x projected hosted-only cost over 12 months (customer will consider reserved capacity).

Workload profile and model choices
- Primary model: mid-sized chat model (approx 7B) quantized; occasionally fall back to 13B for complex queries.
- Typical request length: prompt 180 tokens, completion 70 tokens. Embeddings used for retrieval (50–500k calls/day).
- KV-cache hit expected ~25% for assistant flows; checkout scoring has low reuse (near 0%).

Options considered
1) Hosted-only (Redwood API)
  - Pros: fastest path to launch, no infra for customer to manage, built-in autoscale, streaming support.
  - Cons: cost can spike during flash sales, data residency restrictions require regional hosting (EU region), limited HSM/KMS integration for fully private key custody.
  - Fit: Good for early functional POC and fall-through, not ideal as sole production mode for strict data custody.

2) Dedicated (reserved Redwood capacity in EU region)
  - Pros: predictable throughput, reserved GPUs for peak periods, more control over model variants and runtime configs, supports SLAs, can attach enhanced logging.
  - Cons: commit required (monthly), still not customer-managed network (not fully private), limited direct KMS/HSM options vs Private.
  - Fit: Strong candidate for production checkout scoring (latency SLOs) and cost predictability.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem package)
  - Pros: full data residency and custody, customer-managed network, HSM integration, air-gapped if required.
  - Cons: longer setup (4–8 weeks), ops ownership by customer, more expensive ops+support, patching/migration cadence coordination.
  - Fit: Required if customer insists on keys/data staying in their VPC; otherwise reserved for regulated flows.

Recommended architecture: Hybrid primary Dedicated + Private for sensitive flows, Hosted for burst overflow
- High level: deploy Dedicated pool in EU as the primary serving tier for NorthStar production traffic. Deploy a Private instance for checkout scoring that processes PII-sensitive data and key-managed scoring requests. Host a lightweight Hosted fallback route for overflow during flash-sales (burst absorb).
- Routing logic:
  - Normal traffic: route to Dedicated (cost efficient, reserved capacity).
  - PII-scored requests: route to Private instance (customer VPC endpoint) via policy-based routing.
  - If Dedicated pool reaches 85% utilization or latency degrades above target, automatically failover non-PII assistant requests to Hosted (warm standby).
  - If Private becomes unavailable, queue scoring requests with TTL 10s and send to Dedicated only after explicit opt-in (customer decision).

Design details and tradeoffs
- Latency: Dedicated GPUs proximal to customer region yield stable p95/p99. Private instance must be right-sized for scoring to meet p99 targets; recommend 1:1 capacity headroom of 2x for scoring nodes.
- Cost: reserved Dedicated reduces unit cost per token vs Hosted. Private has higher fixed costs; allocate scoring only into Private to minimize Private footprint.
- Security: use per-route encryption and mTLS between Redwood control plane and Private connector. KMS/HSM integration via customer-managed key ring. Audit logs from Private must be forwarded into customer SIEM; implement log redaction prior to leaving customer network if needed.
- Observability: surface token-level cost and latency in Redwood Console per route. Create a dashboard for: Dedicated utilization, Private latency p99, Hosted overflow calls, cache hit rate, retry/fallback events.

Autoscaling and capacity planning
- Dedicated pool: scale policy configured on CPU/GPU utilization + pending queue length. Aggressive scale-up on flash sale detection (via webhook from NorthStar traffic manager).
- Warm standby Hosted: keep a minimal concurrency reservation during predicted sale windows to reduce cold-start penalties.
- Private: horizontal scaling with pre-warmed instances for scoring; vertical scale limited by model size and quantization.

Rollout plan (90-day PoC -> production extension)
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): functional smoke test on Hosted with sample traffic; validate embeddings and assistant prompts.
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): deploy Dedicated pool in EU, migrate non-PII assistant flows; run synthetic load tests to validate p95/p99.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): deploy Private scoring cluster, integrate KMS/HSM, connect audit log sink.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable hybrid routing and automatic fallbacks; run chaos tests (simulate Dedicated outage).
- Phase 4 (ongoing): capacity reservation negotiation and SLA finalization; establish runbook and SLO alert thresholds.

Success criteria (POC)
- Assistant p95 <= 120ms on Dedicated at 80 RPS baseline.
- Checkout scoring p99 <= 200ms on Private under 2x expected scoring load.
- Fallback to Hosted completes within target SLA for non-PII flows, with <1% failure on test war-room exercises.
- Cost delta vs hosted-only estimated <= 1.4x for 12-month projection given reserved commitment.

Open questions / customer decisions needed
- Confirm whether checkout scoring payloads are allowed to transit Redwood Dedicated if encrypted with customer-managed keys (decision impacts whether Private is strictly required).
- Confirm max tolerated TTL for queued scoring requests during Private outage.
- Will NorthStar accept periodic connection health pings from Redwood into their VPC for routing decisions?

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Dedicated underprovisions for flash peaks -> Mitigation: dynamic burst to Hosted + pre-signed traffic shaping by customer traffic manager.
- Risk: Private deployment delays -> Mitigation: begin Private provisioning in parallel with Dedicated phase when contract signed.
- Risk: Cost overrun during initial months -> Mitigation: enable cost caps, token-level alerts, and a temporary rate-limit policy.

Test matrix (what we will exercise)
- Load tests: baseline, 2x, 5x, and flash-surge 10x for 10 minutes. Measure p95/p99, queue latency, error rates.
- Failover tests: Dedicated -> Hosted failover for non-PII flows; Private outage behavior for scoring.
- Security tests: KMS integration verification, SIEM log ingestion, penetration baseline.

Action items (owners)
- Asha: finalize Dedicated sizing recommendation and draft reserved capacity ask (due 2024-12-07).
- Luca: run initial synthetic load scripts and share results (JIRA-NS-1250) (due 2024-11-20).
- Priya: scope Private provisioning checklist and KMS integration steps (due 2024-11-26).
- Tom: create Console dashboard mock (latency/cost per route) and link to PoC board (done 2024-11-15).

Appendix: rough cost sketch (order-of-magnitude)
- Hosted-only (projected annual): $420k (baseline + burst egress).
- Dedicated (reserved, with 30% utilization smoothing): $310k + Private incremental $85k/year (small scoring cluster) -> combined $395k.
- Notes: numbers are coarse; need billing team for exact SKU mapping.

Next review
- Design review scheduled 2024-12-09 with NorthStar and infra leads. Please bring the Dedicated sizing doc and KMS checklist.

Notes / freeform
- Customer impressed by our failover story during workshop; their security team wants more detail on HSM integration.
- Consider a short one-pager describing the hybrid route semantics for their legal/compliance team (I can draft).
